lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in 24 months = A$100 (Aalders, June 2026) / 1.22 = 81.97, round down to A$80. Leonard Joel A$1,800 excluded (much larger, specialist, category guide). Flip: likely resale about A$100 hammer (single close sale), less 15% vendor commission (assumed for a local auction room) = A$85, no postage (sell locally, collect) = A$85 / 2.44 = 34.8, round down to A$30. Asking prices not used.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification of type from photos, but no size given, only one close SOLD entry (size and condition unknown), and the rest is category guide or dealer asking.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. Dyad Artisans upgraded from snippet only to page opened (price and size confirmed). Persian Rugs entry: GST statement corrected (page says Ex. GST) and design is palmette, so kept only as a category guide ASKING. Leonard Joel kept as SOLD but category guide only, excluded from maximum bid.
lots.key_photo_findings: Five photos. Classic Bakhtiari kheshti panel layout with cypress, willow and boteh-type medallion compartments and cartouche border. Photo 5 shows the back with visible hand-tied knots, confirming hand-knotted. Pile is low across much of the field with abrash and softened, slightly faded colours; some areas look worn close to the knots in photo 4 border. Fringes short or worn. No label or size marker visible.
lots.condition: Used vintage condition: low and uneven pile, some wear patches, worn fringes, colours mellowed. No holes seen in photos but underside not fully shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: What are the exact dimensions? Any holes, moth damage, repairs, stains or bare patches down to the foundation, and are both ends and fringes intact?

Flip: likely resale = median close SOLD about A$175 hammer, less 15% vendor commission (assumed, A$26.25) and A$30 local van or trailer allowance to take it to a room = A$118.75 / 2.44 = 48.7, round down to A$45. lots.key_photo_findings: Four photos. Rectangular mahogany top with canted corners and thumb-moulded edge, deep apron with a winder keyhole visible in the end (photos 2 and 3), so wind-out mechanism. Join line across the top (photo 4) shows a leaf fitted. Bold turned baluster legs on castors. High-gloss finish suggests later re-polish. No drawer, no labels.
lots.condition: Looks sound and well polished in photos; possible re-polish; leaf count, winder handle and mechanism not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the winder handle included and does the mechanism wind smoothly? How many leaves come with it, and what are the closed and extended lengths? Any splits, loose legs or missing castors?

lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos. Nameboard reads 'Mason & Hamlin' in gilt stencil with two roundel (medal) devices either side, legible in photo 3. Compact case on a separate folding trestle stand with two treadles and straps, turned side handle on the cheek (photo 2), gilt stencilled floral decoration on cheeks and front rail. About 49 keys. Several white key tops chipped or missing (bare wood visible near middle), some keys sit unevenly. Lid/music rest present.
lots.condition: Worn original finish with scuffs; missing or chipped key tops; playing order, bellows and reeds unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does it play: do the treadles pump air and do all keys sound? Are the bellows and treadle straps intact, how many key tops are missing, and does the stand fold? Any serial or style number on the back or inside?
